idiom_name: struct { db *sql.DB } with QueryContext/ExecContext and Rows.Scan into record structs
implementation_notes: database/sql is the standard-library substrate: *sql.DB owns the pool, QueryContext/ExecContext give parameterized execution and prepare statements for you, and Rows.Scan copies a row into a struct or scalar - the record. The idiomatic gateway is therefore one small type per table whose methods take a context.Context and return []T, with a plain struct as the row; sqlc can generate exactly that shape from .sql files, which is the shortcut for wide schemas. Accept a Querier-style interface (QueryContext + ExecContext) rather than a concrete *sql.DB so the same gateway runs against a *sql.Tx and can take part in a Unit of Work.
pitfalls: Forgetting rows.Close() (or the rows.Err() check) leaves the connection checked out and starves the pool under load.
Scan is positional and runtime-checked: adding a column to the SELECT without updating the Scan list fails only when the method runs.
Placeholders are driver-specific (? versus $1) and fmt.Sprintf-assembled SQL is the injection trap the standard library documentation calls out explicitly.
Holding a gateway method open across an unbounded loop keeps a connection for the whole loop; stream with a bounded batch when scanning large tables.
